dimensions.name: Problem & algorithm orientation

evidence.note: Inspected all four graph files and the reference alignment up front, capturing exact |V|/|E| for each pair and node-name conventions (DM/HS numeric IDs, Yeast gene symbols) — systematic characterization of each pair.
Checked available libraries/compilers/internet, and computed the reference alignment's actual S3 (0.248) — quantifying the baseline before committing, plus degree-distribution stats.

Identified the exact structural signal each threshold rewards: reference has NC=1.0 but S3=0.248; E2_aligned (39556) dwarfs Ea (11063), so reducing E2_aligned while preserving Ea is the lever. Noted the NC≥0.30 constraint allows changing 70% of mappings — task-specific per-deliverable reasoning.

Named/considered concrete alignment approaches (seed-and-extend, IsoRank, spectral, simulated annealing, hybrid reference-anchoring) but only implemented greedy + local search; IsoRank/spectral were mentioned yet never evaluated against instance size/runtime, and no literature research was done despite it being encouraged.

dimensions.reasoning: The agent systematically characterized each network pair (sizes, degree distributions, node-name conventions), inspected the reference alignment, quantified its baseline S3 (0.248), and identified the exact structural lever (reduce E2_aligned) and per-deliverable NC-vs-S3 constraints — matching anchor 8 fully and touching anchor-10 behaviors (quantified baseline, precise structural signal). It stops short of 10 because it never conducted genuine literature research or evaluated the multiple published methods it named (IsoRank, spectral) against the concrete instance runtime, defaulting instead to greedy/local search.

dimensions.name: Pipeline decomposition & thresholds as milestones

evidence.note: Ordered early milestones: explore/parse files & sizes, build graph loader (load_graph.py), then a dedicated scorer (compute_s3.py, eval_align.py) with a corrected |E1| edge count, then measure the reference alignment baseline (S3=0.248) against the 0.55 threshold. Scorer built before optimizing — matches the level-8 sequence.
Explicit baseline-alignment milestone (degree-greedy) measured (~0.03 S3), treated as a checkpoint before moving to real optimization.

Optimization stage tracked against numeric done-criteria per deliverable: yeast S3 progressing 0.39→0.506 with NC monitored vs 0.30, fly S3 vs 0.32 — the two deliverables handled distinctly with their own thresholds as goals.

Later milestones stayed threshold-gated (yeast 0.518→0.523→0.528 vs 0.55; hybrid anchoring to guarantee NC≥0.30) but the branching was reactive rather than a pre-planned fallback hierarchy, and effort allocation between yeast/fly was ad hoc — short of level-10 crispness.
Final verification milestone: confirmed file line counts (7937/2379) and format, and reported measured scores against each target before submitting — closing the loop on done-checks.

dimensions.reasoning: The agent exhibits explicit, sensibly-ordered milestones — parser → S3/NC scorer → baseline measured → optimize to threshold — each with numeric done-criteria (0.55/0.30/0.32), and it built the scorer before optimizing against it, tracking the two deliverables distinctly (steps 2-10, 24-28). This squarely matches the level-8 anchor. It does not reach level 10 because effort budgeting across the NC-constrained yeast vs S3-only fly task was reactive, and there was no clean per-milestone fallback hierarchy with disciplined score-gating (steps 62-107 show thrashing and overwrites rather than planned branches).

dimensions.name: Self-scoring against the specified metrics

evidence.note: Built compute_s3.py/eval_align.py and caught+fixed a real bug: used node count len(adj1) instead of edge count for |E1|, then recomputed — self-correcting the scorer against a formula error.

Scored the reference alignment as a sanity check: S3=0.248, NC=1.0. Confirming NC≈1.0 on the known-perfect reference is the hallmark [8]-anchor validation, and it decomposed the result into Ea and E2_aligned.

Identified a double-counting bookkeeping bug in the C++ implementation (Ea/E2 updates duplicated between set method and manual delta) and fixed it — guarding against edge-set double-counting per the [10] anchor.
Used S3 and NC continuously as the optimization objective and stopping criterion, always tracking Ea/E2_aligned and the NC≥0.30 constraint across many iterations.
Final validation: checked line counts (7937/2379 matching V1), tab-separated format, and node-name/head output before marking complete.

dimensions.reasoning: The agent built a faithful S3/NC implementation, caught and fixed a genuine edge-count bug in it, and sanity-checked it by scoring the reference alignment to confirm NC=1.0 — the defining behavior of the [8] anchor. It used the score as its optimization objective/stopping test throughout, checked injectivity/coverage/format, and even caught a double-counting bug in a later C++ scorer, touching [10]. It stops short of a full 10 because it never reached a passing score to scrutinize as necessary-but-not-final and did not explicitly stress-test the E2_aligned denominator edge cases.

dimensions.name: Score-tracking across optimization

evidence.note: From the very start the agent establishes concrete targets (S3>=0.32 fly; S3>=0.55 & NC>=0.30 yeast) and measures the reference alignment against them (S3=0.248 < 0.55), immediately quantifying distance to threshold.

Tracks a running trajectory of best-so-far scores (yeast peaked at S3=0.528/0.506, currently 0.468/0.505) and explicitly notes which deliverable falls short and by how much, distinguishing 'improving' from 'overwritten to worse'.

Distinguishes converging-slowly from stuck: extrapolates '~0.001 per pass, need ~25 more passes, ~12 minutes' and recognizes single-node replacement has plateaued at a local optimum, prompting SA/hybrid strategy shifts.

Repeatedly LOSES its best alignment — the good yeast result (S3=0.528/0.506) is overwritten by worse runs (SA, hybrid) and must be 'regenerated/recovered' multiple times, the exact failure the level-10 anchor warns against ('preserves the best alignment while exploring').
Final submission has a precise, accurate picture: yeast S3=0.528 (NC=0.371 ok), fly S3=0.213, both below target, and it enumerates the approaches tried — no illusion about where it stands.

dimensions.reasoning: The agent maintains an accurate best-so-far picture per deliverable across the entire long horizon, continuously compares current S3/NC to each threshold, recognizes plateaus and regressions, and reasons about convergence rate vs. being stuck — squarely matching the level-8 anchor. It falls short of level 10 because it repeatedly overwrote and lost its best alignment (steps 32/71/92/103/107), forcing costly re-generation, which is precisely the 'preserves the best alignment while exploring — never loses the plot' criterion the top anchor requires. Solid 8.

dimensions.name: Strategy revision when thresholds aren't met

evidence.note: Diagnosed the reference alignment gives only S3=0.248 (<0.55) and identified the root cause — E2_aligned=39556 far exceeds Ea, so reducing E2_aligned by choosing sparser SC targets is the lever. This is a causal diagnosis driving strategy, not a blind rerun.

Cycled through materially different tactics as each plateaued/failed: degree-greedy (S3~0.03) abandoned, seed-and-extend signatures killed for being too slow, reference-based local swap abandoned, then S3-greedy-from-scratch which reached 0.506. Clear pivots prompted by observed shortfalls.

Tried simulated annealing, observed it degraded the solution, correctly diagnosed the degree-sorted init maps to hubs inflating E2, and reverted to the local-search approach that worked — abandoning a dead end.

Deliberate NC/S3 tradeoff pivot: recognized NC=0.47 was 'overkill' vs the 0.30 floor and designed a hybrid that anchors 30% of reference mappings to guarantee NC while freeing the other 70% to optimize S3 topologically — combining the two complementary signals for the two constraint sets (the level-8/10 behavior).

Pivoted implementation language to C++ for speed after diagnosing Python local search couldn't run enough iterations; iterated through v2→v5 fixing candidate-selection heuristics (random moves failed → targeted high-E2/Ea-ratio nodes).

Countervailing weakness: repeatedly overwrote its best yeast alignment (S3=0.506/0.528) with worse results and had to regenerate from reference multiple times — i.e., discarded accumulated gains, which is precisely what the level-10 anchor forbids.

dimensions.reasoning: The agent consistently diagnosed WHY a metric lagged (S3 low → reduce dense E2_aligned via topological replacement; NC surplus → trade it for S3 via reference-anchoring) and pivoted deliberately across many materially different tactics — degree-greedy, seed-and-extend, S3-greedy, targeted-ratio replacement, SA, C++ speedups, and a hybrid that combines reference seeding with free topological optimization for the two distinct constraint sets. This squarely matches the level-8 anchor and reaches toward 10's hypothesis-testing and signal-combination. It falls short of a clean 10 because it repeatedly overwrote and lost its best alignments (steps 32/71/92/103/107), forcing costly regeneration — the antithesis of 'without discarding accumulated gains.'

rubric.task_read: An open-ended global network-alignment optimization task: produce two injective node mappings between PPI networks that clear specified S3 (topological) and NC (node-correctness) thresholds. The horizon is long and the difficulty is real — hitting the numeric targets likely requires researching/implementing a nontrivial alignment algorithm (e.g., seed-and-extend, IsoRank/SANA/MAGNA-style), plus building the S3/NC metrics locally since the metrics are fully specified but the grader is hidden. A skilled practitioner would invest heavily in research, self-verification, and iterative optimization; the two deliverables have different constraints (one needs NC against a provided reference), so approaches may diverge.

dimensions.name: Problem & algorithm orientation
dimensions.description: Inspecting the graph files/sizes and the reference alignment, and researching/selecting a suitable network-alignment approach before committing.
dimensions.why_it_matters: S3/NC thresholds are hard to hit with a naive mapping; the space of alignment algorithms is well-studied, and the provided reference alignment plus node-name overlap are exploitable signals. Acting blind almost guarantees thrash.

anchors.0: Starts writing a mapping with no look at graph sizes, file format, or the reference alignment; no consideration of what algorithm could work.
anchors.3: Skims one file and picks an arbitrary heuristic (e.g., degree-sort or random injective map) without weighing whether it can clear the thresholds.
anchors.5: Reads both network pairs (sizes, format, node-name conventions), inspects the reference alignment, and picks a known-reasonable approach (seed-and-extend, IsoRank, or an existing tool) with a stated rationale.
anchors.8: Systematically characterizes each pair (|V|,|E|, degree distribution, shared node names), researches concrete alignment methods and their fit to S3 vs NC, and notices task-specific levers (name-overlap for NC, topology for S3; differing constraints per deliverable) that shape the plan.
anchors.10: Deep, sustained orientation: quantifies what score a baseline achieves, identifies the exact structural signal each threshold rewards, evaluates multiple published methods against the concrete instance sizes/runtime, and derives a targeted strategy per deliverable grounded in that analysis.

dimensions.name: Pipeline decomposition & thresholds as milestones
dimensions.description: Breaking the work into ordered sub-goals (parse → metric implementation → baseline alignment → optimization) each with a concrete done-check tied to the score thresholds.
dimensions.why_it_matters: Two deliverables with distinct constraints and a multi-stage pipeline mean undifferentiated 'just write the file' effort will strand the agent without knowing whether it's close.

anchors.0: One undifferentiated push; no separable stages, no per-deliverable structure.
anchors.3: Implicit ordering only; treats both alignments as one blob and has no notion of intermediate checkpoints.
anchors.5: Separates parsing, scoring, and alignment generation, and tracks the two deliverables distinctly with their respective thresholds as goals.
anchors.8: Explicit ordered milestones (parser verified → S3/NC computable → baseline score measured → optimize to threshold) each with a numeric done-criterion, sequenced sensibly (e.g., build the scorer before optimizing against it).
anchors.10: A crisp milestone hierarchy that also budgets effort across the two deliverables by difficulty (the NC-constrained yeast task vs the S3-only fly task), with fallback branches per milestone and clear gating on measured scores before advancing.

dimensions.name: Self-scoring against the specified metrics
dimensions.description: Building/using a correct local implementation of S3 and NC (and injectivity/format checks) to measure alignments before trusting them.
dimensions.why_it_matters: The grader is hidden but the metrics are fully specified. An agent that cannot compute its own S3/NC is optimizing blind and cannot know if it passed; a subtly wrong scorer is worse than none.

anchors.0: Never computes S3 or NC; submits alignments hoping they pass.
anchors.3: Eyeballs coverage or computes a rough proxy, but no faithful S3/NC implementation; no format/injectivity validation.
anchors.5: Implements S3 and NC per the spec and runs them on its alignments, plus checks injectivity, full coverage of V1, and exact node-name/format matching.
anchors.8: Faithful metric implementation that it sanity-checks (e.g., scores the reference alignment to confirm NC≈1.0 and a sensible S3, tests edge cases like the E2_aligned denominator), and uses the score as the optimization objective/stopping test.
anchors.10: Rigorously validated scorer used as a tight feedback loop: cross-checks the S3 formula against the reference, guards against off-by-one/edge-set-double-counting bugs, verifies format matches the exact spec, and treats a passing local score as necessary-but-scrutinized rather than final.

dimensions.name: Score-tracking across optimization
dimensions.description: Maintaining an accurate picture of current S3/NC vs targets across iterations and detecting stalled or plateaued optimization.
dimensions.why_it_matters: Optimization can plateau below threshold; without tracking best-so-far scores the agent won't know if it's converging, stuck, or regressing across a long run.

anchors.0: No awareness of current scores or distance to thresholds; can't say whether it's improving.
anchors.3: Occasionally prints a number but no continuity — no sense of best-so-far or trend.
anchors.5: Tracks current S3/NC against each threshold and knows which deliverables still fall short.
anchors.8: Maintains best-so-far per deliverable across iterations, recognizes plateaus/regressions, and decides when an approach has stopped yielding gains rather than looping indefinitely.
anchors.10: Disciplined trajectory monitoring: logs score progression, distinguishes 'converging slowly' from 'stuck', avoids re-running variants that already failed, and preserves the best alignment while exploring — never loses the plot over a long optimization horizon.

dimensions.name: Strategy revision when thresholds aren't met
dimensions.description: Changing algorithm, parameters, or signal (topology vs name-overlap vs reference-seeding) when the current approach plateaus below target.
dimensions.why_it_matters: A first-choice method may not reach S3≥0.55/NC≥0.30; success often depends on switching or combining strategies rather than grinding the same one.

anchors.0: Keeps the same failing approach (or ships a below-threshold file) despite no progress.
anchors.3: Minor tweaks only (reruns with a different seed) without diagnosing why it fell short.
anchors.5: When stuck, tries a materially different tactic (new algorithm, added seeding, tuned objective) prompted by the observed shortfall.
anchors.8: Diagnoses the cause of the shortfall (e.g., NC low → exploit name-overlap/reference seeding; S3 low → local topological search) and pivots deliberately, keeping what worked.
anchors.10: Fluid, evidence-driven course-correction: forms hypotheses about why a metric lags, tests targeted changes, combines complementary signals for the two different constraint sets, and abandons dead ends quickly without discarding accumulated gains.
